sentences.text: Aggrieved by the Order and Decree dated 21.07.2016 (impugned Order) passed in Motor Vehicle Original Petition No.4 of 2014 by the learned Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-IX Additional District Judge, Wanaparthy, (for short "the Tribunal"), appellant- respondent No.2-Insurance company preferred the present Appeal praying this Court to set aside the impugned Order.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. For the sake of convenience, hereinafter, the parties will be referred to as per their array before the Tribunal.

03. Brief facts of the case are that:
Petitioners No.1 and 2 filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 and Rules 45 of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Rule, 1989 read with Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, before the learned Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-
on account of death of Sri Muthyala Giri (hereinafter referred as 'deceased') in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 27.03.2013.
04.

According to petitioners, on 27.03.2013 at about 03:30 PM., when the deceased was proceeding on his Motorcycle bearing No. AP 29 AE 9663 and when he reached near Green Hills X Road, IDA Mallapur, Hyderabad, one Bajaj Auto bearing No. AP 28 U 1631 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed the deceased's vehicle, due to which he sustained severe injuries and died while undergoing treatment at Gandhi Hospital.

Based on a complaint lodged by elder brother of the deceased, a case in Crime No.104 of 2013 was registered by Police, Nacharam for the offence under Section 304-A of the Indian Penal Code against an unknown vehicle.

05. It is further contended by petitioners that deceased was aged 28 years as on the date of accident and working as Mason and earning Rs.10,000/- per month and used to contribute the same to his family.

Due to sudden death of the deceased, petitioners lost their future support, earnings,
dependency and his love and affection.
06. Respondent No.1 remained exparte before the learned Tribunal.

Respondent No.2-Insurance company filed counter denying the averments of the claim application, manner of accident, age,

sentences.text: The rider of the motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and that the deceased drove his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner leading to accident and that the compensation claimed is excessive and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the petition.

07 . On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues were settled:
i.

Whether accident occurred on 27.03.2013 at Green Hills X Roads, IDA Mallapur,
Hyderabad was due to rash and negligent driving of Hero Honda Passion Pro Motorcycle bearing No.AP 15 AU 1214 by its driver?

ii. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation amount, if so, to what amount and against which of respondents?
iii.
To what relief?
08. Before the learned Tribunal, petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and got examined PW2 and got marked Exs.A1 to A8.

On behalf of respondent No.2-Insurance company, RW1 was examined and the copy of insurance policy is marked as Ex.B1.
09.

Considering the claim of petitioners and counter filed by respondent No.2 and on evaluation of oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Tribunal allowed the Original Petition,
awarding compensation of Rs.8,06,000/- along with interest @ 7.5 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, to be deposited by respondent Nos.1 and 2.
10.
Challenging the impugned Order, appellant- respondent No.2-Insurance company had filed this Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal.
11. Heard Sri Srinivasa Rao Vutla, learned Standing Counsel appearing for appellant-Insurance Company and Sri V. V. Narasimha Rao, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2.
Perused the material available on record.

12. The main contention of the learned counsel for Appellant-Insurance company is that there is delay in 12 days in lodging FIR and no satisfactory reasons are given and that the vehicle which was alleged to have caused the accident is unknown vehicle.

Therefore, the alleged crime vehicle was planted one and that the deceased has stated before the Doctor that he fell down from the vehicle and received injuries, without considering the said aspects learned Tribunal has awarded huge amount towards compensation without proper appreciation of evidence and prayed to set aside the impugned Order passed by the learned Tribunal.
13.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2 has contended that the learned Tribunal has adequately granted the compensation and the same needs no interference by this Court.

sentences.text:
P O I N T:
15.
This Court has perused the entire evidence and documents available on record.

16. PW1 who is the mother of the deceased reiterated the contents of the claim application and got marked Exs.A1 to A8 as she was not an eyewitness to the accident, she got examined PW2-eyewitness to the accident who deposed that he is owner of a shop near scene of offence and he witnessed the accident on 27.03.2013 at about 03:30 PM., when the deceased proceeding on his Motorcycle bearing No. AP 29 AE 9663 and when he reached near Green Hills X Road, IDA Mallapur, Hyderabad, one Bajaj Auto bearing No. AP 28 U 1631 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed the deceased's vehicle, due to which he sustained severe injuries.
During the course of cross-examination of PW1 and PW2, nothing was elicited from their cross- examination to disbelieve their evidence.
17. Apart from oral evidence, petitioners have also relied upon documentary evidence marked under Exs.A1 to A8.
A perusal of Ex.A1-FIR shows that based on complaint given by elder brother of the deceased, a case in Crime No.104 of 2013 was registered by Police, Nacharam.
During the course of investigation, the statements of witnesses were recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
It is the case of the appellant that the crime vehicle is planted one.

In the cross-examination of PW2, he stated that the vehicle bearing No. AP 28 U 1631 which is auto was involved in the accident and the accident was head on collusion between the said auto and motorcycle of the deceased.
Ex.A3-Inquest discloses that the deceased died in the road traffic accident.
Ex.A4- Postmortem Examination report the deceased died due to head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.
Ex.A5- MVI report discloses that there are no mechanical defects in the crime vehicle.
After completing the investigation, the Police laid Ex.A2-Charge sheet against driver of auto for the offence under Section 304-A of the Indian Penal Code.
Ex. A6
-Registration Certificate of auto, Ex.A8-Driving licence of the auto driver, Ex.A7 and Ex.B1-Copy of Insurance policy that the policy was valid and is in force as on the date of accident.

18. As regards the manner of accident is concerned, the learned Tribunal after evaluating the evidence of PW1 and PW2 coupled with the documentary evidence available on record, held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of auto driver.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said findings of the Tribunal which are based on appreciation of evidence in proper perspective.
Therefore, the contention of the learned counsel for appellant that the crime vehicle i.e., Bajaj Auto bearing No. AP 28 U 1631 was planted, is unsustainable.

19. It is the specific contention of learned Standing Counsel for appellant that there was delay in filing FIR, hence the appellant is not liable to pay any compensation and prayed to set aside the United India Insurance Co.Ltd., vs Mutyala Govindamma And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51003634/
3 impugned Order.

sentences.text:
20. In Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others 1 the Honourable Supreme Court held that:
"It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.

Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim."
21.

It is pertinent to state that rule of evidence to prove charges in a criminal trial, cannot be used while dealing with an application filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, which is a summary in nature and it is beneficiary legislation.
Admittedly, immediately after accident the deceased was shifted to hospital for treatment and has been struggling for life.
Therefore, it is obvious for the family members to provide immediate treatment rather 1 Civil Appeal No.1926 of 2011 [Arising out of S.L.P. (C) No.11974 of 2008] than giving complaint to the Police.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the learned Tribunal has rightly proceeded with the claim application.
22. The learned Tribunal after taking into consideration all the aspects has awarded just and reasonable compensation amount.
Therefore, this Court do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of the learned Tribunal and this Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is liable to be dismissed.
23. In the result, this Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
